extracted.intended_audience: people who want to create or edit nLab pages (mathematicians, students, and contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and conventions for creating, editing, linking, typesetting, and maintaining nLab wiki pages (including LaTeX/iTeX usage, page naming, references, uploads, redirects, and community procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of [[double brackets]] for links
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to other pages are placed in [[double brackets]].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hit “edit page” to see how pages are coded. Use the Sandbox to warm up. There is no preview feature: submit edits and then edit again. Two successive submissions with same signature within 30 minutes count as one.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to start a new page (link request workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a new page, first add a link [[your new page name]] on some existing nLab page (usually in 'Related entries'), submit that edit, then click the question mark on the resulting gray link to open the edit pane for the new page and submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one existing page should refer to the new page; use the Sandbox if you can't think of one. There is no preview: keep cycling Submit/Edit until satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing edits
rubrics_metrics.description: When you edit a page, put your name (with normal capitalisation and spacing) in the box after 'Submit as' so your contribution is credited to you instead of 'Anonymous'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After your first edit your name appears at the bottom as a gray question mark inviting you to create a user page. To create a user page prior to modifying content, make a trivial Sandbox edit to get your name at bottom and click the question mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page titles should contain only ASCII characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Page titles should contain only ASCII characters for ease and to help automatic redirects (remove accents etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and tricks: use links with math-mode or use redirects to present non-ASCII display text. Exception: common European letters (Latin-1) are tolerated for names (e.g. Kurt Gödel). If you need true symbol display, hack using math or create redirects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page titles should be singular nouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer singular nouns for page titles (e.g., [[category]] not [[categories]]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: want only one page per concept despite grammatical variations. Tricks: use link text or redirects to show plural forms when needed. Exceptions exist for sentence-like theorem titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page titles should be uncapitalized
rubrics_metrics.description: Page titles should be uncapitalized except for words that are always capitalized (e.g., [[homotopy theory]] not [[Homotopy Theory]]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use link text to present capitalized forms in running prose. Exception: pages named after specific categories should use capitalised singular abbreviated form (e.g., [[Set]]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as contradicted, use standard American English spelling conventions (e.g., [[center]] not [[centre]]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reason: much of the nLab content is from Urs Schreiber who generally uses American English. Use redirects or link text when alternate spelling is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking new pages from at least one relevant page
rubrics_metrics.description: When you create a new page, ensure it is linked to from at least one existing relevant nLab page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This both guides readers to your entry and helps search engines index the nLab. Example: link a new manifold entry from the manifold-related pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure pages with sections/subsections
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage authors to structure pages by sections and subsections as indicated in the Template page, even when the page is small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subsection structure aids growth and collaborative contributions by guiding where new authors add material and helps reader orientation. Use the Template page for recommended structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include actual mathematics in appropriate environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages should include actual mathematics in appropriate environments (definition, theorem, proof, etc.) as familiar from textbooks and research articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LaTeX-style environments (supported as of mid-2018) for best results. This improves readability and compatibility with LaTeX export.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LaTeX-style theorem/proof environments
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX-style environments such as \begin{theorem} ... \end{theorem} and \label{SomeTheorem} are supported and recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of available environments is provided (definition/defn, theorem/thm, proof, proposition/prop, remark/rmk, corollary/cor, lemma/lem, notation/notn, terminology, conjecture/conj, scholium, assumption, example, exercise, statement). Use labels for referencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels and references for theorem-like environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels (\label{SomeTheorem}) inside theorem/etc. environments create anchors for referencing exactly as in LaTeX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \ref for same-page references to insert the number and hyperlink; this also works when exporting to LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid older 'Instiki' syntax unless necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: An older non-LaTeX syntax for theorem environments exists but is fragile and requires exact labels and whitespace patterns; prefer LaTeX-style syntax where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older syntax needs exact tokens like defn, thm, cor and requires a whitespace after the closing =-- or the parser will ignore content. Use LaTeX syntax to avoid these pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-link central keywords liberally
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperlink central keywords (ideally each and every keyword when it occurs first) to other nLab entries rather than assuming readers share your background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you explain something using other technical terms, provide links to their definitions. This helps readers and search/indexing. When creating a new page, make sure it is linked from at least one related page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide enough context for notation and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because there is no global convention, make sure that when you use notation you provide enough context so intended conventions are clear (e.g., parenthetical remark 'where we use here the convention that...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using notation for the first time on a page, add a parenthetical remark or similar explanation so readers can understand your meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: iTeX differences from LaTeX (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The nLab uses itex2MML with custom hacks; iTeX is not LaTeX and has important differences that affect math input and rendering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read and apply the listed safe workarounds for the specific differences (see the more specific items: identifiers, numbers, operators, whitespace, relations, non-ascii).

rubrics_metrics.name: iTeX: letters without spaces form a single identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: In iTeX’s math mode, a string of letters without spaces is interpreted as a single identifier (so $h=gf$ renders h = gf, not h = g f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want separate identifiers use spaces (e.g. $h = g f$) or use standard LaTeX operator macros (e.g. $\sin(x)$). For custom operator names use \operatorname{Poly}.

rubrics_metrics.name: iTeX: use braces for exponents and numeric superscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers like $10^10$ produce different results in iTeX; the safe syntax is to always use braces: $10^{10}$.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also be careful with punctuation inside numbers; use braces or spaces to avoid unintended parsing (e.g., $t^{3}.2$ vs $t^{3}.2$ issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: iTeX: operator names and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Operator names composed of letters may be combined (e.g. $cos$ becomes an operator). Use backslash \cos for standard operators or \operatorname{Poly} for custom names; if you don't want an operator name, insert spaces between letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using \operatorname ensures consistent rendering in both iTeX and LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: iTeX: whitespace in embedded \text
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitespace around \text{...} behaves differently—iTeX may swallow fore/aft whitespace. Use explicit spacing like \; or \;\text{and}\; when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: prefer $x\;\text{and}\;y$ to ensure desired spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: iTeX: two-character relations and safe alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Two neighbouring relation symbols are not automatically combined in iTeX, so $y := f(x)$ may render with separate ':' and '='.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use $y \mathrel{:=} f(x)$ or the better $y \coloneqq f(x)$ when available to get correct relation spacing and rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: iTeX: non-ASCII characters inside math
rubrics_metrics.description: iTeX assumes strange characters are generated via iTeX commands; it will not parse math with non-ascii characters. Embedding non-ascii inside \text{...} may fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workarounds: break \text command (e.g., \text{in~}\infty{-categories}) or use numbered entities (named entities) where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to make less-than and greater-than signs in math
rubrics_metrics.description: The characters < and > are treated as HTML; in iTeX math mode use \lt and \gt respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: $0\lt 1$ produces 0 < 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get accented characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use HTML/XML/SGML character entity references (e.g., é) or numerical codes (e.g., 㒫) for accented or special characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Toby's complete list of HTML and XML character entity references is referenced; better to use iTeX commands for mathematical symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating links to subsections (anchors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a section header with an anchor using: ## Heading {#anchorname} and then link to it with [[some page#anchorname|link text]] or [link text](#anchorname) for same-page links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor tag must be at the end of the header line. Single-bracket links allow math expressions while double-bracket texts do not. Automatically generated anchors exist but using manual anchors is encouraged to avoid breakage when pages reorganize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbered definition/proposition/theorem anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: In LaTeX-style syntax use \label inside the theorem/etc. environment to create anchors. In older syntax include #name in the environment header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to them via [[some page#theoremname|see this theorem]] or use \ref for same-page references to insert the number and hyperlink.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation numbering and referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: To make an equation automatically numbered use the display-bracket form \[ ... \]; add \label{SomeEquation} and refer with \eqref{SomeEquation}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: only word characters allowed in LaTeX display labels (hyphen '-' cannot be used); use alternatives like \label{FooBar} instead of \label{foo-bar}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents: recommended usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2019, the recommended way to make a table of contents is to write \tableofcontents at the top (or where desired); almost any page should have a TOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An older method using '* table of contents {: toc}' exists but the \tableofcontents command is preferred. Ensure section headings don't contain wiki-links (links inside TOC entries are not allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: References section and citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: Each nLab entry should end with a section '## References' or '## Literature' containing a bullet list of references in a standard formatted way (including optional arXiv/doi links).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format is given with an anchor {#LastnameAnotherlastnameYear} and citation style: see ([Lastname & Anotherlastname Year, theorem 1.3](#LastnameAnotherlastnameYear)). All nLab pages include a 'Cite' link producing a BibTeX entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments and questions should go to nForum
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, use nForum ('Discuss this page' link) to make comments and ask questions, rather than putting query blocks on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the page's discussion thread exists, add a comment there; otherwise start one selecting 'Latest changes' and title same as the page. Query boxes on pages are discouraged (they are often unnoticed); record conclusions of nForum discussions on the page itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use query boxes sparingly; prefer nForum
rubrics_metrics.description: Query boxes (+-- {: .query} ... =--) place a question on the page itself but are generally the wrong way to ask; they clutter pages and go unnoticed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only for brief questions that have been discussed on nForum and where recording the unsatisfactory conclusion with a link to nForum is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standout boxes for permanent emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: To make important text stand out, use a standout box (+-- {: .standout} ... =--) as a permanent emphasis (e.g., an important theorem or slogan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standout boxes are for permanent page features, unlike query boxes which are temporary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including one page within another
rubrics_metrics.description: Include content of page 'foo' into 'bar' by typing [[!include foo]] in 'bar'; the included page's contents are inserted verbatim at that point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included content has no surrounding whitespace and can break formatting (e.g., if included file begins/ends with div tags). Use inclusion for repeated sidebars or messy code (e.g., raw SVG) to avoid cluttering the host page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uploading files and images (file workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: To upload a file, type [FileName](/nlab/files/filename.xyz) or [[FileName.xyz:file]] in an edit, submit, then click the gray link to open the upload dialog and follow instructions; uploaded files reside at /nlab/files/FileName.xyz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pictures use :pic syntax or imagefromfile block for more configuration. For pdf references use description 'pdf' so link text shows (pdf). There is a size limit; steering committee may intervene if upload is abused. After upload you may need to edit the page to refresh due to a bug.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use imagefromfile JSON block for image options
rubrics_metrics.description: To configure images after upload use an imagefromfile block with JSON-like parameters (file_name, width, height, unit, float, margin, alt, caption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults exist for many parameters. Use float and margin to wrap text; if using negative top margin, give a positive bottom margin to avoid caption overlap. Be judicious when floating images (mobile readability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use redirects for pluralisation and capitalization variants
rubrics_metrics.description: To redirect alternate/title variants (e.g., plurals or capitalization) insert [[!redirects othername]] at bottom of the canonical page so linking to othername redirects to the canonical title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: add [[!redirects categories]] at bottom of [[category]] to redirect. Redirects only work when the redirected page does not already exist. For symbol-containing titles, use redirects for nicer link text; note caveats with non-ascii symbols in links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undoing a redirect (creating separate entry)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a redirect exists but you want a separate entry, edit the target page and remove the [[!redirects somepage]] line so you can create somepage normally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer or reorganize material from existing pages as necessary to avoid conflicts and preserve history by renaming old pages to '... > history' when moving content.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle parentheses in hyperlink URLs
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Instiki link syntax uses parentheses, URLs containing parentheses must escape them as %28 and %29, or use an HTML <a href> tag, or use reference-style links ([id]: url).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference-style links require unique ids and are error-prone when copy-pasting; escaping is often simplest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merging pages: preferred community process
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer to raise merge proposals on nForum, check community agreement, and have someone perform the merge rather than unilaterally merging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you merge on your own: edit the kept page A (merge content), add '[[!redirects B]]' to A, copy B's redirects to A, then empty B, rename B to 'B > history' via 'Change page name' (avoid submitting immediately), ensure software's automatically added '[[!redirects B]]' is removed and replaced with 'see [[A]]', then submit with an explanatory announcement. Pages cannot be deleted by regular users; they can be orphaned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removing a page: use nForum request
rubrics_metrics.description: To remove a page, make a request at the nForum rather than attempting deletion via hacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The steering committee or community will handle removal/orphaning procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to deal with nLab spam protection 'Access denied' editing errors
rubrics_metrics.description: nLab uses spam blacklists (spamcop.net, spamhaus.org) which may block your IP; the nLab cannot remove your IP from these lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the blacklist pages, update anti-virus, if on dynamic IP try reconnecting to obtain a new IP. The nLab will not remove spam protection; you must resolve blacklist issues yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to deal with nLab internal errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If the software bails out or produces internal errors, log the error message at nForum with as much information as possible (IP, time/date, URL attempted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View page source to extract additional info; some errors are due to malformed input on edit and that information can help you fix it yourself.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to search the nLab
rubrics_metrics.description: Use conventional search engines with 'site:ncatlab.org' or the built-in search box (which uses regular expressions and searches page source).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instiki search interprets special regex characters; escape special characters (e.g., backslash parentheses) when searching for literal characters like parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular expressions guidance for Instiki search
rubrics_metrics.description: Instiki uses Ruby regular expressions; special characters include . | () [] \ ^ { + $ * ?. Use escapes for literal matches. Provides constructs like \b, character classes [a-z], quantifiers (*, +, ?, {m,n}), alternation, and grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condensed guidance helps craft effective search expressions; be careful with special characters and use escapes when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing nLab pages in external editors
rubrics_metrics.description: You can edit nLab pages in external editors via browser extensions (Emacs, Sublime, Atom, VSCode, Vim) or using editor add-ons that enhance textareas (e.g., Find & Replace for Text Editing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Emacs snippet is provided for users who want to edit nLab content with LaTeX-mode settings and other conveniences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing a page
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'Print' link at the bottom of the page or the Alt-Shift-P shortcut (on many browsers/OS) to go to the printable page view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a printer-friendly rendering of the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customization and themes (user-side)
rubrics_metrics.description: Users can customize nLab appearance (fonts, edit box size) via browser add-ons like Stylish and install available stylish themes (nLab Stylish theme, nLab – nCafe style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Themes by community members change fonts and color schemes to improve readability and editing experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downloading a local copy of nLab content
rubrics_metrics.description: Current git repositories exist for the source content and compiled HTML: https://github.com/ncatlab/nlab-content and https://github.com/ncatlab/nlab-content-html.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these repos to get local copies of pages or to work offline; they are kept current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math diagram tools (TikZ and xymatrix) and caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: nLab supports TikZ (compiled server-side into SVG) and xymatrix for commutative diagrams; prefer TikZ unless you have a preference for Xymatrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikZ code is compiled server-side and included as SVG, so it cannot interact with Instiki code (cannot be nested inside bullet items or math environments); align TikZ code to left of edit window to avoid instiki indentation conflicts. Examples and a quiver editor (q.uiver.app) are suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Older workarounds for diagrams (arrays/matrices) - avoid if possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Older techniques use arrays/matrices or manual hacks to simulate diagrams; TikZ or Xymatrix are preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples using \begin{matrix} and \array are provided, but the guide recommends TikZ where possible for cleaner results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be judicious with floating graphics (responsiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Floating graphics to the side may be harder to read on mobile; consider placing graphics below paragraphs on smaller screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If floating, adjust margins and bottom spacing to avoid captions being obscured by wrapped text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Template page for page organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Template page for recommended section layout and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps make pages consistent and easier for collaborators to add material in appropriate places.
